description: §15.11.4 / §17.1 (S460 F1, positive twin of callback-prop-show-guard-reject) — the same three shapes under `if=` ARE absence-safe: an `if=` element does not exist while its condition is false, so its own attributes (`title=${fmt()}`), its handlers (`onclick=onGo()`) and its children's handlers are never evaluated when the prop is `not`. Compiles without E-TYPE-031. The instances that omit the props render none of the guarded elements; the instances that pass callbacks call them on click (2).
rationale: §17.1: "When `expr` evaluates to false, the element is NOT rendered. It does not exist in the DOM." §42.3.5 lists the `if=` markup guard as a canonical presence-discrimination; §17.2 excludes `show=`.
